source_evidence.anchor: E1: expectation of X:Omega->Real; omitted brackets
source_evidence.observation: Random variables are real-valued; expectation is the Lebesgue integral; E XY means E(XY).
On a given probability space, L2 membership means finite second absolute moment.
E(XY) is the L2 inner product and the norm is the square root of the second absolute moment.

source_evidence.observation: Covariance is separately defined using centered variables; the selected claim is uncentered.

binders: X and Y, universally quantified as random variables in L2 on the same probability space. [E2,E4]
hypotheses: X in L2 and Y in L2; each L2 norm is finite. [E2,E3]
definitions_and_conventions: Expectation is the Lebesgue integral of X:Omega->Real. [E1]
implicit_context: No separate XY in L1 hypothesis is stated. [E4]

details: Every X,Y in L2 on the same probability space are covered. [E2,E4]
Only finite L2 norms, equivalently finite E|X|^2 and E|Y|^2, are required. [E2,E3]
The right side is norm(X,L2)norm(Y,L2) with constant 1. [E4]
No independence, centering, equal-distribution, positivity, or nonzero-norm assumption is stated. [E4]
Zero and almost-surely-zero variables are not excluded. [E4]

undebatable_constraints: X and Y range over L2 random variables on one probability space. [E2,E4]
The right side is norm(X,L2)norm(Y,L2) with constant 1. [E4]
E(XY) is uncentered and cannot be replaced by covariance. [E3,E5]
No independence, mean-zero, positivity, identical-distribution, or nondegeneracy hypothesis may be added. [E4]

ambiguities.issue: The passage does not explicitly say whether L2 elements are functions or equivalence classes modulo almost-sure equality.
ambiguities.evidence: PDF pp.1-2, printed pp.5-6: Lp is called a vector space of random variables and L2 a Hilbert space, without explicitly stating an almost-sure quotient.
ambiguities.impact: A formal carrier may use functions or equivalence classes, affecting equality and carrier semantics, though the numerical inequality is invariant under almost-sure equality.

contract_plain_english: On one fixed probability space, every pair of real-valued random variables X,Y with finite second absolute moments satisfies |E(XY)|<=(E|X|^2)^(1/2)(E|Y|^2)^(1/2). The product is uncentered, the constant is 1, and no independence, centering, positivity, or nondegeneracy condition is imposed. [E1-E5]
